It centers native conditional quantiles on the Gaussian-process mean while retaining the original Gaussian dependence and GP-based eligibility. Real accepted scores update both models and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add the measured full-coordinate adapter exclusively to the native residual predictor, then subtract the adapted distribution’s own integrated mean before adding the unchanged Gaussian-process location. This exposes previously constant count coordinates through unit-count offsets while preserving native transforms on variable coordinates. Unlike the earlier adapter experiment, mean ranking cannot change on a common state; unlike the parallel shape and scale interventions, the adapted residual keeps its own shape and scale. The experiment identifies this joint adapter-and-location variant.

finding_summary.headline: Residual adaptation increased generating-parent gains but remained below the Anchor
finding_summary.insights: Holding GP location fixed allowed the imported adapter to improve full-run purchase gains without reviving the earlier, refuted native-location ranking hypothesis. The borrowed quantile integration and exact variable-column preprocessing both operated, but the campaign uses constant tails and an identity full-width filter, so published predictive claims do not transfer to this experiment. The complete adapter changed 1,440 paid identities against filtered inputs, while nonzero constant-coordinate values changed 247 against a same-width zeroed reference. That locates two observable input effects but does not assign their separate score contributions: the passive branches have no alternative adaptive histories. Same-paid pinball loss was 0.020571 for the active law, 0.020736 for filtered inputs and 0.020571 for zeroed constants; these small calibration differences cannot explain the gain by themselves. The full gain increase also did not cure late progress or establish reliable endpoint benefit. Chemistry narrows the remaining method limitation: the >=60-heavy-atom tail shrank from 384 to 112 proposals, yet productive diversity remained uneven, including one high-score aromatic-amide stream concentrated in one generic framework versus five before. Other streams retained broad framework diversity, so universal scaffold collapse is unsupported. Reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and cyclic allenes persisted or increased, and 1,836 proposals had unspecified stereocentres. These observations support examining a proposal operator that preserves coherent ring/linker units and represents bond environments, rather than assuming another residual adjustment alone will resolve chemical quality. They do not establish that those liabilities caused the score changes. This result settles the registered conditional full-gain test; the separate input-channel contributions, sustained late utility and the broader approach remain open.
finding_summary.results: The adapter operated in all 435 allocations with no fallback, while GP means, eligibility, copula draws and selector randomness stayed fixed on each shared state. Against the passive filtered-native reference, it changed 2,122 paid positions and introduced 1,440 purchases outside the reference selected set. All 1,405 such purchases with a next-fit opportunity entered both real models; the remaining 35 were terminal. Total positive gain over actual generating parents rose from 14.21298 to 16.68613 across all 4,350 purchases, so the registered useful-residual prediction is confirmed. Ten of fifteen cell gains increased. The late 2,175 purchases weakened, however: gain fell from 4.44597 to 3.91565. Endpoint mean was 0.562256, versus 0.558989 for the code Parent and 0.607030 for the formal Anchor. The paired code-Parent increase was 0.003268, with seed deltas +0.006556, -0.023717 and +0.026963; the Anchor difference was -0.044774, so the required +0.002 Anchor goal was not met. Docking endpoint gains offset losses in the fluorinated-ring task, which declined in every seed. Native allocation work took 4,548.46 candidate-clock seconds versus 1,640.73 in the Parent; the two passive residual references added a separately measured 6,091.10 seconds.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic products shrink the large-size tail, but reactive bonds, strained rings and unresolved stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-ada68e100737 produces substituted fused heterocycles, aryl carbonyl compounds, polycyclic amines and highly fluorinated nitrogen-rich rings. It is not missing rings: the digest gives ring-closure rates 0.9839–1.0 and aromatic-text rates 0.9609–1.0 over the five optimizer streams. Common conventional motifs coexist with N–halogen/O–halogen bonds, N–S/N–N linkers, cyclic cumulenes and highly compressed ring systems. Chemical makeability remains questionable; parsing and a high recorded score do not establish isolability, synthetic access or activity. There are no synthesis, stability, pKa or experimental binding measurements in this evidence. The proposed missing features below distinguish observed score-associated assemblies from chemistry-quality gaps; no hidden target structure or named pharmacophore is inferred. Child evaluation and code-Parent pairing are both complete in the frozen comparison. All fifteen Child trajectories and fifteen published Parent trajectories were read: each arm contains 4,500 accepted records, including 4,350 optimizer proposals and 150 initial records. No requested task, seed, path or Parent comparison is missing. The digest final-molecule excerpt is not a final Top-1 list and mainly shows the last seed; per-seed maxima and final proposals were therefore checked in the full trajectories. All 4,350 optimizer SMILES in each arm parse with RDKit 2023.09.6. RDKit descriptors, computed on every optimizer purchase without deduplication, give Child heavy atoms 1–117 (median 29), compared with Parent 1–120 (median 30). The <=6-atom tail is 23 versus 23; the >=60-atom tail is 112 versus 384. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1,814/1,123 versus 1,951/1,305; these count graph variation, not independent productive chemotypes. Mean maximum initial-molecule similarity is 0.264357140 versus 0.244004738, using Morgan radius 2/2,048-bit Tanimoto within each session and excluding molecules with <=6 heavy atoms on both sides; this is an initial-archive proximity descriptor, not a novelty or contribution verdict. Child/Parent proposal counts containing N–halogen bonds are 719/704, O–halogen bonds 269/161 and cyclic carbon allenes 191/96. All Child proposals have unspecified stereochemistry in the digest; RDKit flags unassigned centers in 1,836 Child proposals and assigned centers in none. Neutral notation alone does not mean absence of protonatable amines. These associations cannot identify the adapter, location consumer or another retained component as the chemical cause. Evidence and definitions: policy/scratch/r0064-03-improve-L01/molecular-pooled-descriptors.json; policy/scratch/r0064-03-improve-L01/molecular-source-manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0064-03-improve-L01/molecular-audit.py. The manifest hashes the immutable request and all thirty source trajectories. Child snapshots preserve exact trusted staging bytes; they grant no additional SMILES citation authority. Only per-task high-score strata are interpreted; combined cross-task top30 fields in the audit are not comparable across objectives.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly compact aryl carboxamides built around an indole-like fused core. Optimizer molecules span 8–47 heavy atoms, with median 24 and median three rings. The seed-0 winner is an alkyl/methoxy indole carboxamide with N-chloro amide and bromopyridyl substitution; seed 1 instead reaches an anilide on a benzocyclobutene-like core; seed 2 favors an N-hydroxy anilide attached to a substituted indole bearing N–S or N–halogen groups. The best thirty pooled proposals occupy four typed scaffolds but only one generic scaffold, compared with seven/five in the Parent. Overall variation is therefore broader than the productive core family. The basic aryl-amide motif is synthetically recognizable; the unusual nitrogen substitutions and strained carbocycle make several leaders questionable. liabilities: 130 of 870 proposals have an N–halogen bond, including 20 of the highest thirty; such bonds require chemical scrutiny rather than being treated like ordinary aryl halides.
Several leaders carry N–S/S–halogen appendages or a strained fused carbocycle. The very large coupled indole products are poor-scoring size extremes.
missing_features: The leading set lacks a comparably productive range of conventional replacements for its N–halogen/N–S substitutions while retaining the aryl-carbonyl arrangement. That is a chemical plausibility gap; the observed scores do not establish a required extra pharmacophore.
Productive core diversity is limited: the highest thirty proposals reduce to one generic framework, despite broad lower-scoring graph variation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.305104808; the seed-2 N-hydroxy anilides reach 0.461957846. Both excessive assembly and severe truncation fare poorly: the 47-heavy-atom joined indole product scores 3.3811572294260344e-18, and difluorobenzene scores 2.2064040954992307e-13. A late direct aryl-linked product lacking the carbonyl/N-hydroxy linker scores 0.183170478, consistent with preserving a moderately sized carbonyl-linked aromatic assembly rather than adding rings indiscriminately. N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-bromo indole variants tie at 0.461957846, so this stream does not resolve their chemical liabilities. The Parent likewise produced substituted indole amides, but also high-scoring bicyclic hydrazine/lactam and annulated heteroaromatic alternatives. Observed endpoint comparison to n-e2506e11f536: seed 0: Child 0.438799247, Parent 0.449897262, signed delta -0.011098016; seed 1: Child 0.403312176, Parent 0.445453991, signed delta -0.042141815; seed 2: Child 0.461957846, Parent 0.435540579, signed delta +0.026417267. These are paired endpoint associations, not chemical-component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: Large, mostly aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies dominate: median 44 heavy atoms and five rings, with a 1–117-heavy-atom range. The seed-2 winner has seven rings and 52 heavy atoms: a conjugated pyrimidinedione-like center joined to multiple phenyl, pyridyl and diazine rings through an anilino/aryloxy substituted alkene. Seed 0 reaches a different 52-heavy-atom, nine-ring assembly with repeated nitrogen-rich dione units. Seed 1 instead carries a halogenated fused nitrogen-rich dione with imine/imidate groups, N–Cl and O–Br. These are materially different chemotypes, not one shared endpoint. The Parent also made oversized heteroaromatic assemblies; its seed-1 winner was a more compact fused azaaryl product. Conventional subfragments are recognizable, but overall synthesis and stability are uncertain. liabilities: 218 of 870 proposals contain O–halogen bonds and 123 contain N–halogen bonds; the seed-1 winner has both. These are different from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.

Large polyaryl/dione structures combine synthetic complexity and substantial aromatic surface; solubility and reactivity were not measured. Six <=6-heavy-atom proposals and 73 >=60-heavy-atom proposals expose both size extremes.
missing_features: The sampled set does not establish a compact, chemically conventional realization of the useful heteroaryl/carbonyl arrangement across seeds. The observed direction favors connectivity and heteroatom placement, not an identified missing target-specific group.
Stable alternatives to the O–Br/N–Cl and elaborate imidate/imine motifs are poorly represented among the successful seed-1 products.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Isolated F, Cl and the short azine C=NN=C all score 0.5; preserving connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies raises the stream above that floor. The seed-2 extended multiaryl product scores 0.632454162, while the largest 117-heavy-atom product scores 0.577865525. Late addition of another heteroaryl substituent gives 0.607727797, so size or aromatic ring count alone is not the gradient. The high-score pool is larger than the Parent high-score pool (highest-thirty heavy-atom medians 52.5 versus 30), even though the entire Child stream has far fewer >=60-atom products (73 versus 346). This distinction matters: reducing the large tail did not produce uniformly compact winners. Observed endpoint comparison to n-e2506e11f536: seed 0: Child 0.608359133, Parent 0.608081247, signed delta +0.000277886; seed 1: Child 0.593641678, Parent 0.628461587, signed delta -0.034819908; seed 2: Child 0.632454162, Parent 0.598225779, signed delta +0.034228382. These are paired endpoint associations, not chemical-component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: This stream has recognizable amine-rich medicinal-chemistry features: aromatic hydrophobes joined to saturated or partially unsaturated nitrogen-containing rings. Median size is 30 heavy atoms, median ring count five, and median aromatic ring count two. The seed-0 winner is a 28-heavy-atom sulfoxide-containing benzofused ring system linked to a second aryl/saturated amine ring system; seed 1 favors a substituted pyrrolidine/diarylmethyl amine with an N-chloropyrrole; seed 2 produces a compact bridged polycycle carrying an amine and thiophenol substituents. The highest thirty proposals all carry nonaromatic amine motifs and span fourteen generic scaffolds, so missing basic amine centers or wholesale scaffold collapse would be incorrect descriptions. Every member of that high-score subset has unassigned stereocentres. liabilities: The whole stream contains 233 N–halogen-bearing proposals, although none of the pooled highest thirty carry that flag; useful chemistry and problematic side exploration coexist.
Thiophenols, a stereogenic sulfoxide and intricate bridged rings raise oxidation, stereochemical and synthesis questions. Neutral SMILES do not resolve the protonation state of the amines.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical definition is absent from the high-scoring ring systems, including sulfoxide-bearing and multiply substituted polycycles. The observations cannot determine which stereoisomers would retain their scores or be accessible.

Chemically ordinary analogues preserving the demonstrated aryl/amine arrangement without N-chloropyrrole, free thiols or difficult bridged topology remain an unresolved plausibility opportunity; no missing basic amine requirement is supported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 sulfoxide/amine assembly reaches 0.999997429; the smaller sulfoxide ring derivative with a hydrazino substituent at evaluation 270 scores 0.001171093. The N-chloro carboxamide/sulfonamide fragment scores 0.00016650955053713697, and a 109-heavy-atom ester/acetal/sulfonamide conglomerate scores 0.028858377. Thus the observed gradient associates appropriately connected aromatic and amine-bearing ring systems with better scores, while neither an amine-like group alone nor molecular bulk suffices. In seed 2, a 23-heavy-atom bridged/thiophenol product reaches 0.993721231; further aryl/thiol elaboration at the final proposal gives 0.433466549. The Parent also found amine-containing polycycles, including sulfonamide-containing and tightly bridged examples; the Child chemical changes are seed-dependent. The scores do not measure experimental affinity or identify a binding mode. per_task.generated_character: The dominant chemistry combines propyl/ethoxy-substituted aryl or indole-like groups with nitrogen-rich carbonyl rings, medium rings or bridges. The stream spans 1–73 heavy atoms, with median 32 and five rings. The seed-0 winner contains an aryl ester/acetal-like cyclic motif and a cyclic amide/hemiaminal arrangement; seed 1 gives an annulated azaaromatic system connected to a large amine/carbonyl ring; seed 2 favors an indole linked through N–N to a bridged lactam/ketone system, with related N–S-linked analogues nearby. The highest thirty proposals have 31–39 heavy atoms and thirteen generic scaffolds, compared with six in the Parent: this is exploration of many decorated frameworks, not absence of ring chemistry. Basic functional groups are familiar, but assembly and stereochemistry complicate practical synthesis. N–N/N–S linkage, potential hemiaminal character and complex ring closures warrant stability/synthesis scrutiny. Two of the highest thirty proposals have an O–O bond; a favorable numerical score does not resolve that liability.
missing_features: More productive, synthetically straightforward connections between the aromatic and carbonyl-rich ring portions remain unshown; the leading alternatives rely on N–N/N–S connectors, large rings or bridges. This is a capability gap rather than proof of one absent atom or functional group.

Stereochemical definition and coherent retention of both molecular portions are missing from a substantial fraction of the exploration: truncation gives zero scores, while large multi-core joins are also weak.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methane, ethene, acetylene, water and NNO have recorded score zero. Keeping both aromatic/heteroaromatic and carbonyl-rich cyclic portions gives approximately 0.23; the strongest seed-2 N–N-linked product scores 0.236669016 and the nearby N–S-linked bridged product 0.235112440. Conversely, the 73-heavy-atom multi-core product scores 0.118863898. The initial highest score is 0.167838659, and the generated stream improves through coherent multigroup assemblies, not tiny fragments or unlimited ring addition. The Parent uses related aryl/ethoxy/carbonyl and amine-rich cyclic chemistry; the Child changes linking and annulation patterns but does not expose a uniquely missing pharmacophore. per_task.generated_character: Compact nitrogen-rich fused carbonyl/imino heterocycles with multiple fluorines dominate. Median size is 27 heavy atoms and four rings, over an 8–48-heavy-atom range. Seed 1 reaches an imino/lactam fused core carrying a fluorinated cyclobutene and a hydroxylated cyclobutadiene substituent; a closely scoring alternative instead has a small cyclic cumulene. These structures are fluorinated heterocyclic constructions, not demonstrated realistic analogues of a reference drug. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
